label: #348 part 1
summary: #348 part 1. Fine's PLG rules (The Pure Logic of Ground, p. 5) were read in full (pp. 3-7) from the NYU-hosted PDF; because that host answers CI runners with HTTP 405 and no Wayback fallback could be pinned, FINE-PLG-1-2 is a bibliographic span recording the consulted byte and text hashes for a later web_snapshot upgrade, and encoded as an inductive derivability predicate. Fine's derived rules check out, with one precision: his Amalgamation derivation cuts against `C, C, … ≤ C`, so Cut must allow repeated antecedent atoms and Amalgamation needs a nonempty family. Non-Circularity plus derived transitivity excludes derivable cycles for consistent assumptions and gives well-foundedness on finitely many atoms; a rank countermodel shows it does not give well-foundedness on infinitely many atoms. Source search: deRosset's On Weak Ground (RSL 7, 2014) and Better Semantics for the Pure Logic of Ground (Analytic Philosophy 56, 2015) could not be obtained: PhilArchive DEROWG/DERBSF returned a Cloudflare challenge and web.archive.org was unreachable from the pinning environment; no claim is made from them. Fine's fact semantics, soundness/completeness and deRosset's semantics remain for #349.
